From 1–2 shared root spots at the bottom edge, raise 3–5 slim tall blades per root. Their heights and upward leans vary; they use a fine green brush and draw no ground. Fill each leaf interior with the same color as its outline.

Draw one horizontal gray thick-brush branch slowly undulating through the middle, then join 6–8 closed two-arc summer leaves to distinct points on its performed line. Draw the leaves with a fine green brush and fill the interior enclosed by each pair of arcs with the same green.

Arrange 5–7 slim tall red leaves radially from a palm center in the middle. Each is a rotring two-arc form touching at both ends, with a stem drawn downward from the center. Fill each leaf interior with the same color as its outline.

Place 8–12 fallen leaves in order along a diagonal band from upper left to lower right. Each is a bleeding crayon two-arc form touching at both ends, with strictly alternating red and gray and varied rotations. Fill each leaf interior with the same color as its outline.

From 1–2 shared root spots at the bottom edge, raise 3–5 tall withered blades per root. Heights and leans vary strongly from vertical to falling; gray chalk sways quickly with bleeding edges, and no ground is drawn. Fill each leaf interior with the same color as its outline.
Place 2–4 cloudforms in the lower left or right corners. Their outlines sway finely in gray chalk, and their interiors are filled with the same gray.
